- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.5x recent mean), model overreacts; apply decay factor of 0.85 to subsequent 3-day forecast.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 15%+ from recent peak), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast downward by 5–15% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 7-day average for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underperform; add 5–10% buffer to forecast for next 3 days.
